nodes.text: Easy now. Deep breaths. The Ring runs cold the first morning — it always does. There. You're standing, you're breathing, and you're *here*, which is more than most manage gracefully.

I'm *Rowan*. Elder of Dawnmead, keeper of the Waking Ring — those five old stones you just stepped out of. Folk have been arriving through them since my grandmother's grandmother kept this watch. _Where you were before you woke, nobody remembers. Not you, not any waker before you._ We've stopped asking. The stones don't answer.
Ask what you like. First mornings are for questions.

Dawnmead. A green, a brook, more chickens than people — and past our hedgerows, the *frontier*, as wide as your patience. They say there were more lights out there once. Now there's us, the wayfarers' lanterns along the old roads, and whatever you wakers raise next. Rest here a day, learn what your hands are for, then take the lane. You will too. They all do.

None of you do, child. You arrive with a pack on your back, strength in your limbs, and a name on your tongue — nothing else. _Some say the stones take the memories as toll. Some say you left them behind on purpose._ Either way: what you do NEXT is yours, and no toll can touch it.

Three doors, then the road. *Warden Bryn* keeps the yard south of the Ring — she'll wake up those arms of yours. *Iona* tends the fire by the south cottage — she'll teach you to feed yourself. And your pack is already heavier than you think: axe, pick, blade, bow, and a staff with a little weather in it. Go look. Then come back to me before you take the lane.
Here — {item:bread}, baked before you were… well. Before this morning, at least. Welcome to the world, waker. It's mostly kind, out to the hedgerows anyway.
